paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God doesn't call people because they feel ready. He calls them because He sees. He says, "I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt" (Exodus 3:7), and then He sends a shepherd. Moses asks, "Who am I?" (Exodus 3:11), and God never answers that question. He answers with "I will surely be with you" (Exodus 3:12).

So the question was never who Moses is. It was always who God is. Moses brings excuse after excuse: they won't believe me, I'm slow of speech, please send someone else. And every time, God points back to Himself, to the staff in Moses' hand, and to the One who gave man his mouth (Exodus 4:11). I made excuses too, friend, and I'm not proud of it. I told an angel he had the wrong drawer!

Here's what this means for you, baker. When God asks something of you and your hands feel empty, don't start by counting what you lack. Start with who is asking, because He said, "I AM WHO I AM" (Exodus 3:14), and His name is for every generation (Exodus 3:15). He stays with you, He helps you, and He gives you what you need for the next step. Go with Him, even when your knees are knocking.
